_note: Firmware catalog for the badge site. All hosted builds are served same-origin from firmware/ (browsers CORS-block raw github fetches). Entries with builds[] empty are flashed via their release page + FLASH LOCAL .BIN.

firmware.name: Badge Launcher v2 "Touch"
firmware.desc: The flagship badge experience. One flash + one FAT micro-SD = pick-what-you-run: two touch mesh messengers (MeshCore + Meshtastic MUI), classic Meshtastic, a Reticulum RNode, an NES emulator with 37 homebrew games, and WLEDkitty — switchable from an on-badge menu in ~10 s.
firmware.buildsLine: 1 image, flashable here — then add a FAT micro-SD with the app pack from the release
firmware.note: Hold UP at reset to get back to the launcher from any guest. Nine lives, one badge.

builds.label: the launcher firmware — after flashing, add a FAT micro-SD (unzip sd-card-apps-v2 from the release)

firmware.name: DOOM
firmware.desc: The 1993 classic, natively, full speed — 320x240 fullscreen, shareware WAD memory-mapped out of flash. D-pad moves, A fires, BOOT switches weapons. Audio build plays SFX through the piezo.

builds.label: SFX through the piezo — gloriously PC-speaker

firmware.name: Anemoia NES
firmware.desc: A full NES emulator: drop .nes ROMs on the micro-SD, browse and launch on-badge, play with D-pad + A/B. Save states, chiptune audio through the piezo, curated legally-free homebrew library.

firmware.name: Meshtastic
firmware.desc: Off-grid LoRa mesh messaging with phone app support. Standard, power-tuned (-39% idle), and experimental full color touch UI (MUI) builds. Set your region before use: meshtastic --set lora.region US
firmware.note: ANTENNA FIRST. Never TX on LoRa without a 915 MHz antenna attached.

builds.label: stock behavior, classic button-driven TFT UI
daily driver — idle draw cut ~39%, B = back
color touch UI, on-screen keyboard (BLE off, phone via WiFi/TCP)

firmware.name: MeshCore
firmware.desc: The badge as a MeshCore LoRa mesh node — the flagship build is a standalone touchscreen mesh communicator (chats, contacts, channels, on-screen keyboard, RF monitor + spectrum analyzer) that is simultaneously a BLE companion for the phone app.
firmware.note: Factory images, not launcher SD guests — flash over USB. Hold UP at reset to return to the launcher.

builds.label: the one to use — full touchscreen mesh communicator
radio for the MeshCore phone app (BLE)
companion over USB serial for meshcore-cli / web client

firmware.name: Reticulum / RNode
firmware.desc: Turns the badge into an RNode: a host-controlled 915 MHz LoRa transceiver for the Reticulum network stack (NomadNet, Sideband, MeshChat). TFT build shows a live status screen — frequency, airtime, channel load, signal.
firmware.buildsLine: 2 builds: tft · headless — then provision once with rnodeconf

builds.label: recommended — live RNode status screen on the TFT

firmware.name: rsDeck
firmware.desc: Ratspeak's Reticulum/LXMF messenger ported to the badge as a standalone on-device communicator — touch UI with on-screen keyboard, D-pad + A/B nav, per-conversation drafts, piezo chimes, BOOT = announce. Runs as a factory image or as a ratspeak.bin SD-launcher guest.
firmware.buildsLine: 2 images: standalone factory · ratspeak.bin launcher guest · AGPL-3.0
firmware.note: Defaults to the 914.875 MHz / 125 kHz / SF7 house channel — interoperates with fleet RNodes out of the box. Changeable in Setup.

firmware.name: WLEDkitty
firmware.desc: A WLED fork designed to run on the badge — drive the ten NeoPixel ears (and anything on the NeoPixel-out header) from the WLED web UI or phone app. Boots into a pride rainbow; A/B + d-pad switch effects on the go, with live status on the TFT.
firmware.buildsLine: 1 image, flashable here · also runs as a launcher SD guest

builds.label: standalone WLEDkitty — boots a Pride rainbow; replaces the SD launcher

firmware.name: TempleOS Portable
firmware.desc: Terry Davis's divine operating system goes portable — HolyC, the oracle, and 16-color glory on the badge TFT. God said 640×480 was enough.
firmware.buildsLine: flash from the release page — divine intervention not required

firmware.name: ESP32 Bus Pirate
firmware.desc: A Bus Pirate-style multi-protocol workbench, native on the badge TFT: one CLI (USB serial, Wi-Fi web UI, or browser Web Serial) that speaks I2C/SPI/UART/1-Wire/JTAG and more — with on-screen bus scan + live register monitor, a BME280 environment dashboard that colours the ears by temperature, Wi-Fi/BLE scanners, and on-board LoRa TX/RX (verified badge-to-badge).
firmware.buildsLine: 1 badge-native build · transmit-capable · authorized use only
firmware.note: ⚠ Transmit- & attack-capable: Wi-Fi deauth/sniff, BLE spoof/sniff, LoRa & RF transmit, bus/RF jam. Use ONLY on hardware, networks & RF you own or are authorized to test. Never TX on LoRa without a 915 MHz antenna. I2C targets go on the SAO header (J5), not Qwiic.

builds.label: full multitool — buses + Wi-Fi/BLE/LoRa, on-screen scan & BME dash
